mappings.note: Theme A, the geographical world and maps. C-SST1.2 is the competency whose content that theme carries; no LO names a theme, and LO-1 to LO-4 under it are specific map skills the item does not test.
Theme B, Tapestry of the Past - 'who we are and where we come from'. The history goal CG-SST2, since the item asks what the whole strand is for rather than any one source or period outcome.

Theme C's objective, the foundations of our civilisation and the value of its cultural principles today. That is C-SST4.2's competency statement; C-SST4.2-LO-2 is narrower, listing astronomy, medicine and metals.
Theme D, governance and democracy making responsible citizens. CG-SST3 is that goal verbatim; the C-SST3.2 outcomes are about local bodies, which the item does not reach.

'Multidisciplinary', and the answer's worked example is reconstructing an ancient civilisation from geography, history, archaeology and economics together. C-SST2.1 is the competency about combining source types to reconstruct a period; the frame has no outcome about the disciplines themselves.
'The past is still with us' - why history is studied at all, so the history goal CG-SST2 rather than a source or period outcome.
